note: What a person saw when they looked at each GPU run's stills and frames (the founder's reviewer). A rejected product is still evaluated, so its numbers show the failure, but it gets no renders and is left off the blind page. A faulty product is evaluated and rendered so the fault can be seen, but it is not a panel bundle and is left off the blind page. Verdicts: accepted, faulty, rejected.

azure-palm-baby-doll-dress.why: run 16b (stage 2 + 4 on run 16a's FASHN stills recomposed with stage 1b QA 0.10.1): no grey cap above the sleeves in the stills or in any turntable frame (the residual grey, 78 px per frame, sits at the neck edge); print, puff sleeves, babydoll as in run 15. Open, flagged, not repaired: (1) the recompose grew the garment mask along the whole outline, not only at the caps, and keeps a thin cream tail below the hem of the back still at the mannequin's left (not in run 15's still; missed when the stills were reviewed); stage 2 grows it into a plain cream unprinted flap swinging out at that side of the hem in turntable_b frames about 84-159 (about half the turn, up to ~10 cm at 104-108), which stage 4t fits as a slightly longer, wider back hem; (2) in turntable_a frames about 32-56 the lower skirt on the mannequin's right is translucent, with the grey leg showing through and ragged tips below the hem (smaller in run 15 at 46-50); most of the holdout IoU loss against run 15 sits in frames 40-80; (3) 2 vertices 3.3 mm from the mannequin; (4) the motion clip draws a sleeveless strappy dress (not used). Looked at by the evaluating agent and a reviewer, not yet by the founder; the stills need a re-review at the hem

crimson-wildflower-maxi-skirt.why: kept for evaluation, not for the panel: waistband and print right, but NOT at the hips (the founder: "see the hips"): in both stage 1b stills the grey mannequin hip shows outside the skirt at the sides, and in the stage 2 frames the skirt opens into a wedge-shaped slit at the side with the grey leg showing. Stage 1b QA failed the front only (silhouette 0.864) and was overridden

rosewater-blouse.why: FASHN stills torn (patches of print with the mannequin showing through, the back a pale blotchy shirt); stage 2 frames contain black panels on the back and side. Stage 2 ran anyway because --accept-failed-dress overrides the silhouette and fidelity failures

rosewater-palazzo-pants.why: FASHN drew a closed skirt in both views (legs merged in 259 of 259 rows); the type gate stopped it before stage 2. The shop photo's legs are so wide they read as a skirt

woodstock-wanderer-knit-cardi.why: front still a shrunken bolero (sleeves and a scrap of front), back a white sleeveless top with holes; stage 2 frames show black and grey halves and a garment that changes
